body:
> **Rewritten 2026-07-11.** The first version of this issue was filed prematurely and closed the
> same day. It named `GenerateTupleReturnAliases` as the emitter — **that function is never called
> on this path**, and a guard placed there is dead code. It also described the tail-alignment
> shift, which is the *symptom*, not the root cause. Both are corrected below. The analysis is now
> backed by an end-to-end A/B (same kernel source, only the pypto `.so` varies), a candidate patch,
> a zero-regression sweep over 54 kernels, and a device run.

## Background

`pypto-lib`'s qwen3-14b 40-layer decode (`models/qwen3/14b/decode_fwd.py`) is silently miscompiled:
the orchestration binds a consumer task to the **wrong tensor operand**. Tensor args bind
**positionally** (`L0TaskArgs` appends every `add_input`/`add_inout` into one ordered array; the tag
only selects RAW/WAW/WAR), and the three tensors involved are all BF16 — so nothing type-checks the
swap. It compiles clean, runs, and the in-harness golden (a second on-device dispatch of the same
code path) reports PASS.

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `d5cfab8e` (also reproduced on `8ebddcb8`) |
| simpler | `c94aa9f3` |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| pto-isa | `83d01313` (the pin) |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |

pto-isa is not a confound — this is compile-time orchestration codegen and reproduces byte-for-byte
at the pin.

### Component

Codegen

## Root cause

**The return-position → callee-param map is poisoned before codegen ever sees it.**

A Group/Spmd wrapper around a **multi-result** inner kernel forwards the inner call's whole tuple as
**one** return expression while declaring **N** return positions:

```python
fa_fused (Group):
    self.fa_fused_aic(...)
    result = self.fa_fused_aiv(...)     # TupleType, 3 results
    return result                       # ONE return expr, THREE return positions
```

`return_lineage::TraceVar` (`src/ir/transforms/utils/return_lineage_utils.cpp`) cannot describe that
shape. It resolves a var to a **single** param root, and its user-call branch deliberately bails on a
multi-result callee:

```cpp
if (ret_map.size() != 1 || !ret_map[0]) return nullptr;
```

So `ReturnedParamIndices(fa_fused)` comes back `[nullopt]` instead of `[1,3,7]`. The Spmd wrapper
destructures that poisoned map, `IsReturnedParamMapPrecise()` sees an untraced tensor at position 0
and returns `false`, and the emitter falls back to the **legacy tail-alignment heuristic**:

```cpp
if (!precise) {
  for (size_t i = 0; i < effective_dirs.size(); ++i)
    if (effective_dirs[i] == Out || effective_dirs[i] == InOut) out_indices.push_back(i);
  tuple_out_base = tuple_arity >= out_indices.size() ? (tuple_arity - out_indices.size()) : 0;
}
...
} else if (elem_pos >= tuple_out_base) {
  size_t out_pos = elem_pos - tuple_out_base;
  if (out_pos < out_indices.size()) param_idx_opt = out_indices[out_pos];   // <-- shifts
}
```

The heuristic assumes the returned tuple's tail elements correspond, in param order, to the
Out/InOut params. That breaks as soon as the callee writes an Out/InOut param it does **not** return
— an accumulator, `__gm_pipe_buffer`, an in-place-written KV cache. `out_indices` grows, the returned
tuple stays short, `tuple_out_base` **clamps to 0**, and every returned element binds one slot off.

**⚠️ The emitter that actually fires is `GenerateSubmitReturnAliases`**
(`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp` ~L3466) — **not** `GenerateTupleReturnAliases`.
An instrumented build (one printf per aliasing site) shows **zero** hits in the latter for this
kernel; every call goes through the former, which carries a byte-for-byte copy of the same heuristic:

```
[PB] SUBMIT callee=fa_fused_spmd   precise=0
[PB] SUBMIT callee=fa_work_build   precise=0
```

A guard placed only in `GenerateTupleReturnAliases` is dead code. Both sites need it.

## Actual behaviour — the end-to-end A/B

**Same kernel source. Only the pypto `.so` changes.** Compile-only, `N=2` layers, no device.

Stock pypto (`d5cfab8e`), generated `orchestration/decode_fwd.cpp`:

```cpp
params_t15.add_inout(k_cache__rv_v2);
params_t15.add_inout(v_cache__rv_v2);
params_t16.add_input(v_cache__rv_v2);       // out_proj  <-- WRONG OPERAND
k_cache__rv_v2 = all_q_padded_inline382;    // garbage loop-tail yield
v_cache__rv_v2 = k_cache__rv_v2;
```
```
grep -c "add_input(attn_out"  ->  0     # attn_out is written by fa_fused and read by NOBODY
```

Same kernel, pypto **+ the patch below**:

```cpp
params_t16.add_input(attn_out_inline336);   // out_proj  <-- CORRECT
```
```
grep -c "add_input(attn_out"  ->  1     # the garbage yield lines are gone
```

The remaining `k_cache__rv_` / `v_cache__rv_` lines are legitimate: the params **are** loop-carried
(fa_fused writes them in place) and now correctly alias `ext_k_cache` / `ext_v_cache`.

## Trigger

The conjunction of three conditions. Remove any one and the binding is correct:

- **(a)** a **function-param** tensor rebound by `pl.assemble` inside the task (so it is both a loop
  carry and an InOut of the fused task);
- **(b)** under a **runtime conditional** inside the fused region — in qwen3 it is a lane guard
  (`if rope_lane < ROPE_CORES`, 32 of 48 AIV lanes). This is what makes the Group return the
  forwarded tuple rather than N direct params;
- **(c)** inside a `pl.range` loop of **≥ 2 trips** (a 1-trip loop collapses the carry).

This explains all three control arms of the reproducer, which is the reason to believe the mechanism:

| arm | the Group returns | result |
|---|---|---|
| conditional removed | 3 exprs, each a direct param | **traces fine → correct** |
| the param write moved to its own root | 1 value → `ret_map.size()==1` | **single-result branch works → correct** |
| loop trip count = 1 | carry collapses | **correct** |
| **all three present** | the forwarded tuple | **`TraceVar` bails → mis-bind** |

## Blast radius

qwen3-14b 40-layer decode, graded against the **known-clean pre-fusion parent commit** on one shared
fixture (a golden-independent cross-commit argmax comparison, since the in-harness golden shares the
code path): **4 of 16 batch rows agree**, `max_abs_err` ≈ 5.13, on 12/12 rounds. With the patch, on
the **byte-identical kernel source**: **16/16 on all 12 rounds**, excursions 0/12.

To be precise about what that number is: it is agreement with the pre-fusion parent, not an absolute
correctness oracle. The patched build still differs from that same anchor by `max_abs_err` 0.457 —
a separate, unrelated numerical-faithfulness gap in the kernel, not a codegen issue.

## Relationship to #1573 / #1702

Same recurring root cause — a return-param map that codegen cannot resolve, "fixed" by a positional
guess. **#1702** fixed the single-return path (`GenerateSingleReturnAlias`). **#1573** (closed
2026-05-29, fix landed in `d5cfab8e`) added the precise `GetReturnedParamIndices` /
`IsReturnedParamMapPrecise` path for the tuple case — but its own code comment **explicitly leaves
Group/Spmd wrappers on the legacy heuristic**:

> ```
> // Fall back to the heuristic when the map is not fully trustworthy (Group/Spmd
> // wrappers with no traceable top-level ReturnStmt, or return shapes the tracer
> // cannot model).
> ```

This issue is exactly that leftover. It is not a duplicate: #1573's own reporter kernel
(DeepSeek-v4 `decode_compressor_ratio128.py`) is **already clean** on `d5cfab8e` — it is not a
forwarded-tuple wrapper, so the precise path covers it.

Worth noting for the fix: the in-code comment's premise is also wrong. `fa_fused_spmd` **does** have
a top-level `ReturnStmt`. The imprecision is *inherited* from the Group it calls.

## Proposed fix

**Primary — make the map precise.** Teach `TraceVar` to expand a forwarded tuple position-by-position
through the inner call, and canonicalise the wrapper's single forwarded-tuple return into N explicit
param returns. Patch attached in the PR: 3 files, +130/-3.

Verified:
- fixes the original fused `decode_fwd` (above) and the reproducer;
- **zero regressions**: 53/54 pypto-lib kernels compile before and after (identical set); after
  normalising SSA counter renumbering, **54/54 generated orchestrations are semantically identical**
  — a strict no-op on every kernel whose map was already precise;
- device: 4/16 → 16/16 argmax on the byte-identical kernel source.

**Complementary — fail loudly instead of guessing.** When `precise == false` and the tail-alignment
is genuinely ambiguous, hard-error instead of silently mis-binding. The naive predicate
(`precise == false && >1 Out/InOut param`) is **not shippable** — it trips on `fa_work_build`
(2 Out/InOut params but tuple arity 0, so the heuristic binds nothing and cannot be wrong) and breaks
9 of 44 kernels. The shippable predicate is the clamp itself:

```
fire iff  0 < tuple_arity < out_indices.size()  AND  >1 Out/InOut tensor param
```

`tuple_arity == 0` (nothing aliased) and `tuple_arity == out_indices.size()` (exact order-preserving
alignment) are provably safe and let through.

## Ruled out — please do not chase these

Each was tested and falsified:

- **Not a missing WAR / anti-dependency edge.** `attn_out` has **no reader at all**
  (`grep -c "add_input(attn_out" -> 0`), so there is no hazard to miss. This is a wrong-operand bug,
  not a race.
- **Not an SSA-naming artifact.** The tensor *handles* were traced, not the names; the consumer
  genuinely receives a different buffer.
- **Not `bind_dynamic`.** Falsified twice, including on the real kernel — deleting it changes nothing.
- **Not pto-isa.** Reproduced byte-for-byte at the pin `83d01313`. Compile-time only.
- **Not a runtime/scheduler issue.** Fully visible in the generated `.cpp` with a compile-only run.
title: [Bug] Orchestration codegen: a Group wrapper forwarding a multi-result call's tuple poisons the return-param map, silently mis-binding a consumer's tensor operand (leftover of #1573)

body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** — compiles clean, runs on a2a3, output is all zeros on every written row. A single `pl.matmul` whose FP32 output is materialized into a scope-local `create_tensor` and then **read back per-row and scattered into distinct (strided) GM rows**, all inside one `CORE_GROUP` scope, silently produces zero data on device.

Distinct from the existing reports:
- **#1525** (chained matmul → cast → matmul) explicitly has *no slice* and adds *acc-reuse* between two matmuls. This case has **one matmul**, **no acc-reuse**, and **does** slice (per-row subview) + scatter. Neither contains the other.
- **#1507** (cube→vec bridge drops matmul `valid_shape`, breaking a downstream vec subview) is the closest mechanism — but it is **CLOSED**, and this still reproduces on current `main`, so this is either an uncovered sibling of that fix or a regression on the matmul→store→subview→scatter path.
- Related: #1523, #1352.

### Description

In one `CORE_GROUP` scope (`pl.split(NONE)`):
1. `kv_final[:, :] = pl.matmul(x, w, out_dtype=pl.FP32)` — cube matmul, whole-tile store into a scope-local `create_tensor`.
2. `for b in pl.range(B): cache[b*CACHE : b*CACHE+1, :] = pl.cast(kv_final[b:b+1, :], BF16)` — per-row subview read + scatter to a distinct strided GM row.

Compiles clean, runs (`compile done`, `runtime done`), but the output `cache` is all-zero on every written row (`actual=0.0`, expected nonzero). The cube→vector RAW dependency from the whole-tile store to the per-row reads is dropped: the first reads see uninitialized (zero) data. The result is **deterministic** (same rows zero across runs), not a race.

#### ~30-line repro (`-p a2a3`)

```python
import pypto.language as pl

B = 16
H = 64
CACHE = 256


def build_program():
    @pl.program
    class Repro:
        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Opaque)
        def fused(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[B, H], pl.BF16],
            w: pl.Tensor[[H, H], pl.BF16],
            cache: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[B * CACHE, H], pl.BF16]],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[B * CACHE, H], pl.BF16]:
            kv_final = pl.create_tensor([B, H], dtype=pl.FP32)
            with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.NONE)]):
                kv_final[:, :] = pl.matmul(x, w, out_dtype=pl.FP32)   # cube matmul, whole-tile store
                for b in pl.range(B):                                 # per-row scatter to distinct cache rows
                    cache[b * CACHE : b * CACHE + 1, :] = pl.cast(kv_final[b : b + 1, :], target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint")
            return cache

    return Repro


def golden(values):
    out = (values["x"].float() @ values["w"].float()).to(values["cache"].dtype)
    for b in range(B):
        values["cache"][b * CACHE] = out[b]
```

Observed: `'cache' FAIL`, `Mismatched elements: 1577/262144`, first 20 mismatches all `actual=0.0` vs nonzero expected.

Notes:
- `UP_DOWN` instead of `NONE` does not help: it fails earlier at `SplitVectorKernel requires an even split dimension, got 1` (the per-row `[1, H]` slice cannot be row-halved).
- Reading the matmul SSA value directly (no `create_tensor`) fails ptoas: `'pto.subview' op boxed layout subview sizes must be multiples of inner shape` (single row of the L0C-boxed matmul output).
- Forcing a vector materialize (`pl.mul(acc, 1.0)`) compiles but the whole [B,H] FP32 tile overflows Vec UB.
- An older revision of this repro **deadlocked** on device (`aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018`, `sched_error_code=100`); on the current stack the same code silently miscompiles to zeros instead — same fused-scope bug, two manifestations.

#### Real kernel

`models/deepseek/v4/decode_indexer_compressor.py` — the `kv_hadamard` + `kv_and_cache_write` scopes cannot be mix-fused for this reason. The unfused two-scope form (matmul→GM `kv_final`, then a separate scatter scope) is correct and passes; merging them into one scope produces 3 zero rows in `kv`/`kv_cache`.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `3834f3d` |
| pypto | `78e44c6` (branch: main) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `e03faff` |
| pto-isa | `0f171f73` |
| ptoas | 0.41 |
| CANN | 9.0.0 |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)
title: [Bug] Codegen: cube matmul -> per-row scatter to distinct GM rows in one CORE_GROUP scope silently produces all-zero output

body:
Related: #1042

### Component

Codegen

### Description

`name_hint` supplied to `pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="GetKVCache")` is not propagated to the merged swimlane output. The generated `merged_swimlane_*.json` still uses autogenerated function names such as `func_3_d(...)` and contains no `GetKVCache` string.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In `examples/models/qwen3/qwen3_14b_decode_scope2.py`, annotate the in-core scope as:
   `with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="GetKVCache"):`
2. From the `pypto-lib` repo, run:
   `python examples/models/qwen3/qwen3_14b_decode_scope2.py -p a2a3 --runtime-profiling`
3. Open the generated merged swimlane JSON under:
   `build_output/Qwen3Scope2_<timestamp>/swimlane_data/merged_swimlane_<timestamp>.json`
4. Search for `GetKVCache`.

### Expected Behavior

The merged swimlane JSON and the swimlane view should include the supplied `name_hint` for the annotated CORE_GROUP region, for example an event or function name containing `GetKVCache`.

### Actual Behavior

No `GetKVCache` string appears in the merged swimlane JSON. Event names remain autogenerated, for example:
- `func_1_b(r1t1)`
- `func_0_a(r2t0)`
- `func_2_c(r3t0)`
- `func_3_d(r3t2)`

### Git Commit ID

d7a037746554ecf38e2fe3b118c330510db3f1bc

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Repro annotation site: `/data/liuxu/pypto-lib/examples/models/qwen3/qwen3_14b_decode_scope2.py:221`
- Observed artifact: `/data/liuxu/pypto-lib/build_output/Qwen3Scope2_20260421_175051/swimlane_data/merged_swimlane_20260421_175059.json`
- `GetKVCache` does not appear anywhere in the merged swimlane JSON.
- Sample event names from that JSON: `func_1_b(r1t1)`, `func_0_a(r2t0)`, `func_2_c(r3t0)`, `func_3_d(r3t2)`.
- `pypto-lib` worktree commit at repro time: `b7ebff6f85d4e18cbe249847919d67f36cda51f9`
title: [Bug] CORE_GROUP name_hint is not reflected in merged swimlane JSON

body:
### Summary

A `CORE_GROUP` mix scope (`pl.split(...)`) that fuses a cube op (matmul) with a **per-row dynamic-address GM scatter** on the vec side **compiles clean but deadlocks at runtime with `507018`** (`aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018`). Reproduces under both `SplitMode.NONE` and `SplitMode.UP_DOWN`.

A **dynamic-address READ** and a **contiguous-address WRITE** in the same mix scope are both fine — only the **dynamic-address WRITE** deadlocks (isolation matrix below).

> Note: I have **not** root-caused the mechanism or the owning layer (pypto codegen vs runtime vs pto-isa FFTS). This report is the **reproducible observed behavior + isolation only**; please treat the cause as open.

### Where it shows up

`models/deepseek/v4/decode_indexer_compressor.py`: trying to fuse the `kv_hadamard` (cube matmul) and `kv_and_cache_write` (per-row block-table scatter into `kv_flat` + paged `idx_kv_cache`) scopes into one mix scope.

Pattern (per POST_CHUNK group, NONE mix):

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.NONE)], name_hint="kv_hadamard_cache_write"):
    kv_final = ...                      # cube: hadamard matmul -> [POST_CHUNK, HEAD_DIM]
    for r in pl.range(POST_CHUNK):      # vec: per-row scatter
        c_idx = c0 + r
        if gate(c_idx):
            kv_row = kv_final[r:r+1, :]
            kv_flat = pl.assemble(kv_flat, kv_row, [c_idx*S, 0])                 # contiguous store -> OK
            cache_row = block_table_lookup(c_idx)                                # idx_block_table read -> OK
            idx_kv_cache_flat = pl.assemble(idx_kv_cache_flat,                   # DYNAMIC-ADDRESS store -> 507018
                                            pl.cast(kv_row, pl.BF16, mode="rint"),
                                            [cache_row, 0])
```

### Symptom

- Compiles clean (no codegen error).
- Runtime: `507018` on a2a3. Both NONE and UP_DOWN.

### Isolation matrix (a2a3 device, reproducible)

| Variant in the mix scope | Result |
|---|---|
| matmul + per-row **dynamic-address** scatter (`idx_kv_cache[cache_row]=`) | **507018 deadlock** |
| matmul + per-row **contiguous** write only (`kv_flat[c_idx*S]=`) | runs (no deadlock) |
| matmul + dynamic-address **READ** of `idx_kv_cache[cache_row]` + contiguous write | runs (no deadlock) |
| existing `score_fused` (NONE mix, block-table **reads** + contiguous `score_flat` write) | works |

So the trigger is specifically the **dynamic-address (data-dependent) GM store on the vec side of a mix scope**. Block-table reads and contiguous stores are fine.

### Observation (NOT a confirmed cause)

In the generated `kernels/aiv/kv_hadamard_cache_write_aiv.cpp` for the deadlocking case, the active lane (`get_subblockid()==0`) does the full `TLOAD`/`TSTORE`/dynamic-`TSTORE` with its pipe-flag sequence, while the inactive lane (`else`) takes a structurally different, shorter branch (a degenerate `valid_shape=(0,0)` `TCVT` + `pipe_barrier(PIPE_V)`, no `TLOAD`/`TSTORE`). I'm flagging this asymmetry only as an observation — I could **not** establish that it is the cause of the `507018` (the outer pre/post `set_flag`/`wait_flag` frame is balanced on both lanes), so please don't take it as the diagnosis.

### Asks

1. Support a dynamic-address (block-table-indirected) GM scatter on the vec side of a cube+vec mix scope — or determine it's unsupported.
2. Either way, emit a **compile-time diagnostic** instead of compiling clean and deadlocking at runtime.

### Workaround

Keep the scatter in a separate, non-mix scope (the existing 2-pass design: cube `kv_hadamard` scope → GM hand-off → separate per-batch `kv_and_cache_write` scope). That runs and passes.

### Related

- #1564 (SplitVectorKernel degenerate-subblock) — possibly related (mix dual-lane codegen), but I have not confirmed any connection.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `7e1bbd0a` |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `324df3d6` |
| ptoas | `0.43` (CI pins `v0.41`) |
| pto-isa | `0f171f73` |
| pypto-lib | `25ac6cf` (branch `perf/dsv4-decode-indexer-rope-core-spread`) |
| CANN | 9.0.0 |
| Host | Linux (aarch64), a2a3 |
title: [Bug] Dynamic-address GM scatter on the vec side of a cube+vec mix CORE_GROUP scope deadlocks (507018); dynamic reads + contiguous writes are fine

body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** — IR generation succeeds; codegen aborts on an unmapped accumulator MemRef. Internal `Check failed` (no diagnostic/hint), so this is a codegen scheduling gap, not user error.

### Description

A single `pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP)` scope that chains **two cube matmul accumulator stages with a vector epilogue between them** (cube → vec cast → cube) fails to compile:

```
Failed to compile group 'fused_incore_0': Internal error: no MLIR mapping for MemRef base 'mem_acc_8'
Check failed: it != fs_.memref_to_mlir.end() at src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp:1214
```

Stage 1 (`acc1 = a@w1`, matmul_acc, FP32) is pushed to AIV, cast to BF16, fed to stage 2 (`acc2 = acc1@w2`, matmul_acc). In the final IR the AIV side allocates `mem_acc_8` (16384B) that is **declared once, referenced zero times** — codegen then can't map it and asserts. The `mem_acc` round-trip across the cube→vec→cube boundary is left dangling. Independent two-accumulator scopes (both reading the same input, no vec feeding the 2nd matmul) compile fine — only the *chained* case fails. `pl.split` mode (NONE/UP_DOWN/LEFT_RIGHT/auto_chunk) is orthogonal; all crash identically.

Minimal repro (~40 lines):

\`\`\`python
import pypto.language as pl
M = K = N = 64
@pl.program
class Repro:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Opaque)
    def fused(self, a: pl.Tensor[[M,K],pl.BF16], w1: pl.Tensor[[K,N],pl.BF16],
              w2: pl.Tensor[[N,N],pl.BF16], y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M,N],pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[M,N],pl.FP32]:
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.NONE)]):
            acc1 = pl.create_tensor([M,N], dtype=pl.FP32)
            for kb in pl.pipeline(0,2,stage=2):
                acc1 = pl.matmul(a[:,0:32], w1[0:32,:], out_dtype=pl.FP32) if kb==0 else pl.matmul_acc(acc1, a[:,32:64], w1[32:64,:])
            m1 = pl.cast(acc1, target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint")   # vec epilogue between stages
            acc2 = pl.create_tensor([M,N], dtype=pl.FP32)
            for nb in pl.pipeline(0,2,stage=2):
                acc2 = pl.matmul(m1[:,0:32], w2[0:32,:], out_dtype=pl.FP32) if nb==0 else pl.matmul_acc(acc2, m1[:,32:64], w2[32:64,:])
            y = pl.add(acc2, 0.0)
        return y
\`\`\`

Real kernel hitting this: deepseek/v4 decode_indexer rope_slice+rope_assemble cannot mix-fuse for the same reason. Related: #1352 (acc MemRef base unification), #1507 (cube→vec bridge).

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | \`9b95926\` |
| pypto | \`78e44c6\` (branch: main) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | \`e03faff\` |
| pto-isa | \`0a1ce52\` |
| ptoas | 0.41 |
| CANN | 9.0.0 |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)
title: [Bug] Codegen: no MLIR mapping for mem_acc when a CORE_GROUP scope chains two matmul_acc stages through a vec epilogue (cube→vec→cube)

body:
### Summary

Add cluster-level programming abstractions for inter-core communication within a cluster. The design envisions:

- Dummy tensor allocation at cluster scope
- `allocate_cluster` scope for cluster-level resource management
- `PIPE_IN` / `PIPE_OUT` data movement primitives
- `TPUSH` / `TPOP` operations for inter-core communication

Currently, the `Cluster` class in `src/backend/common/soc.cpp` is a hardware topology model only — no user-facing programming abstraction exists.

### Motivation / Use Case

Cluster-level programming enables efficient inter-core data sharing and pipelining within a cluster of cores on Ascend NPUs. Without these primitives, users cannot express multi-core collaborative computation patterns that exploit data locality within a cluster, limiting performance for workloads that benefit from inter-core communication (e.g., large matrix multiplications, pipeline-parallel inference stages).

### Proposed API / Behavior

```python
# Conceptual API (to be refined during design)
with pl.allocate_cluster() as cluster:
    dummy = cluster.alloc_tensor([1024], pl.FP32)
    pl.pipe_out(src_tensor, dummy)
    pl.pipe_in(dummy, dst_tensor)

    # Inter-core push/pop
    pl.tpush(data, target_core=1)
    received = pl.tpop(source_core=0)
```

### Additional Context

Found during feature audit for user-facing documentation (issue #310). Git commit: `1d217f238b74d54b9f420539c1c39d0a4bba1974`.
title: [Feature] In-cluster function groups for inter-core communication

body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** — compiles clean, runs on a2a3, output is all zeros. Distinct from the matmul_acc crash #1523 (single matmul, no assert; silent miscompile). Shares a root with #1507 (cube→vec valid_shape loss) but no slice involved and adds acc-reuse, so neither contains the other.

### Description

Two chained matmuls in one `CORE_GROUP` scope — cube → vec cast → cube — compile but produce all-zero output on device (4094/4096 mismatch, `actual=0.0`). Each weight is a distinct param (transpose pass#198 clears). Final IR (`37_after_Simplify`):

- Stage1 `t1 = a@w` and stage2 `y = t1b@w2` both write the **same** `mem_acc_9` (offset 0) → 2nd matmul overwrites 1st before consume.
- AIV side: stage2 `tpop_from_aic` carries `valid_shape=[0,0]` → `cast` emits empty tile → `t1b` is zero → `y` zero. No `pl.slice(valid_shape=...)` anywhere.

~40-line repro:

\`\`\`python
import pypto.language as pl
M = K = N = 64
@pl.program
class Repro:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Opaque)
    def fused(self, a: pl.Tensor[[M,K],pl.BF16], w: pl.Tensor[[K,N],pl.BF16],
              w2: pl.Tensor[[K,N],pl.BF16], y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M,N],pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[M,N],pl.FP32]:
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.NONE)]):
            t1 = pl.matmul(a, w, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
            t1b = pl.cast(t1, target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint")
            y = pl.matmul(t1b, w2, out_dtype=pl.FP32, b_trans=True)
        return y
\`\`\`

Real kernel: deepseek/v4 decode_indexer rope_slice+rope_assemble cannot mix-fuse for this reason. Related: #1507, #1523, #1352.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | \`9b95926\` |
| pypto | \`78e44c6\` (branch: main) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | \`e03faff\` |
| pto-isa | \`0a1ce52\` |
| ptoas | 0.41 |
| CANN | 9.0.0 |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)
title: [DX] pypto silently emits all-zero when a pl.Out is reassigned to a detached value in a mix/split CORE_GROUP scope — should be a compile-time diagnostic

body:
In `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py`, the grouped compilation path (lines 502–544) compiles AIC + AIV members into a single ptoas module, then calls `_generate_kernel_wrapper(func, ptoas_cpp)` for each member with the **same full combined ptoas output**. This means both `kernels/aic/<name>.cpp` and `kernels/aiv/<name>.cpp` embed the complete AIC+AIV code, each with a `kernel_entry` that calls only its own function.

When the hardware compiler processes each wrapper in its respective core mode, the dead static functions from the other core type cause compilation failures due to incompatible ISA instructions.
